entries.text: What did your first customers do the second week?
entries.speaker: metrics

choices.text: Seven of ten came back; two needed help and one left.
choices.reply: A cohort and a denominator. We can have a conversation.

choices.text: We have a lot of sign-ups.
choices.reply: A sign-up is a hello. I asked whether they stayed.

choices.text: Our retention is inevitable.
choices.reply: Please put inevitable in the forecast, not the actuals.

entries.text: Who can say yes to buying this?
entries.speaker: metrics

choices.text: The person who does this work also controls the small team budget.
choices.reply: A buyer close enough to the problem to recognise it.

choices.text: Everyone with a computer.
choices.reply: That is a distribution problem disguised as a market.

choices.text: We do not know yet; three buyer calls are booked.
choices.reply: Good. Bring the calls, including the uncomfortable one.

entries.text: What costs more as a customer uses it more?
entries.speaker: metrics

choices.text: Compute and support. We measure both per completed job.
choices.reply: A unit we can count. Please keep counting it.

choices.text: Nothing. The cloud is effectively free.
choices.reply: It has been remarkably effective at sending invoices.

choices.text: We are still measuring inference cost.
choices.reply: An unknown with a measurement plan beats a decorative margin.

entries.text: If the large platforms copy the feature, what remains?
entries.speaker: philosopher

choices.text: The workflow, the permissions and the habit of using it.
choices.reply: A reason to stay that does not fit on a release note.

choices.text: We will move faster.
choices.reply: Speed is an activity. What will it accumulate?

choices.text: We may be a feature; we are testing the wider need.
choices.reply: A small honest question can become a useful company.

entries.text: What would convince you this idea is wrong?
entries.speaker: philosopher

choices.text: If teams still use the old workflow after a month of supported trials.
choices.reply: A belief with an exit door. Encouraging.

choices.text: Nothing; conviction is the moat.
choices.reply: Then this is a faith round. We do not lead those.

choices.text: If nobody pays at the price that covers our costs.
choices.reply: Good. Do not discount away the answer.

entries.text: Why does this work now?
entries.speaker: philosopher

choices.text: The data can finally be exported, and the buyer has a budget for the problem.
choices.reply: A change in the world rather than a change in your calendar.

choices.text: Agents are having a moment.
choices.reply: Moments tend to invoice annually.

choices.text: We have not isolated the change yet.
choices.reply: Then make that your next experiment.

entries.text: Explain the demo without explaining the architecture.
entries.speaker: vibes

choices.text: It turns the missed delivery list into a route the driver can actually use.
choices.reply: I can picture the person and the Tuesday.

choices.text: We orchestrate a multi-agent abstraction layer.
choices.reply: I can picture a diagram arguing with another diagram.

choices.text: It does one useful job, and we can show it.
choices.reply: Excellent. The room has one attention span.

entries.text: What happens when it is confidently wrong?
entries.speaker: vibes

choices.text: It shows its evidence, stops the automatic action and lets a person correct it.
choices.reply: The correction is part of the product. Keep it visible.

choices.text: We raise the confidence score.
choices.reply: The number was not the problem I was asking about.

choices.text: We fall back to the existing manual workflow.
choices.reply: An unglamorous landing is still a landing.

entries.text: Three robots. One bad. Please keep the partners and the good robots dry.
Watch the path and the task. A confident scan is a second opinion, not a verdict.
Clear target, clear reasoning, dry partners. We can discuss the numbers.
Strong energy. Very wet. We will send the carpet invoice separately.
That was the delivery robot. It had a real delivery. We will try again tomorrow.
We would like to invest. The paperwork is longer than the meeting. Your evidence earned another conversation.
We enjoyed meeting you. We will follow up after one more customer conversation. Please keep sending the numbers.
Thank you for the demo. We could not yet connect the problem, the buyer and the price. Bring a concrete customer example next time.
The room is needed for another meeting. Your slot can be booked again tomorrow.
What changes in someone’s day when they use it?
entries.speaker: Mom

entries.text: Who has that problem? Have you asked them, or just other founders?
entries.speaker: Mom

entries.text: When you say revenue, is that money arriving or a person saying it sounds nice?
entries.speaker: Mom

entries.text: You do not have to explain the whole company. Tell me the useful part.
entries.speaker: Mom

entries.text: I understand. It helps that person do that job. Now go and ask whether they want it.
entries.speaker: Mom

entries.text: ok honey. call me
entries.speaker: Mom

entries.text: It is fine not to know. Find out before you make the slide bigger.
entries.speaker: Mom

entries.text: Eat something, get some sleep, and call me when you are not walking into traffic.
entries.speaker: Mom

i moved the meeting. then the meeting moved me
fog is up. good for hiding. bad for pretending we saw everything
the restored one remembered us. i am going to be normal about this
clock stopped. for once that is the good kind of outage
I am trying to deliver the soup before it becomes an architectural solid.
The reminder helps, but I still want a person to check the important bit.
I can approve a small trial. A citywide deployment needs someone else.
Show me one finished task. I have already seen six concept videos.
If it fails, tell me what stopped. Do not just make the spinner friendlier.
My route is fine. The pickup spot is where the problem happens.
The tool is useful when I can undo what it did.
I want the order I placed, not a personalised interpretation of it.
Clear user, repeated task, observed pain. Test willingness to pay before expanding the market slide.
People understand the job. The buyer and the budget are still unclear. Run one paid pilot with a narrow success measure.
The interviews describe a different problem. Keep the notes, revise the question and avoid turning compliments into demand.
The useful surprise was operational: people need a recovery path more than another recommendation.
The useful part of this startup is remarkably well hidden by the startup part.
A bold attempt to make one sentence require a glossary.
A clear user and a clear job. The deck must have felt very left out.
The demo worked. The confidence slide is taking credit for the sprinkler.
Your business model has found product-market fit with your cloud invoice.
The company has pivoted so often the logo is developing steering.
